page: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and includes 472 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

Benchmark data indicates balanced performance across multiple workloads. In single-core evaluations, the server demonstrates strong performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2171.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.31 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is average, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8331.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 7990.62. Memory bandwidth reaches 621.3 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 66.9 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations, measured via Redis SET operations, achieve an average of 12.02 million operations per second.

The hardware configuration presents specific performance tradeoffs. While the CPU's AMX instructions support vector and matrix operations, LLM inference speeds vary significantly. Prompt processing for a medium 7B model reaches an average of 53.73 tokens per second, but text generation for the same model drops to a weak 8.03 tokens per second. Given the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the inclusion of 472 GB of local storage, this server is suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations that benefit from local disk caching without requiring heavy GPU acceleration.
